blocks.text: Documents the deliberate scope boundary: this file covers the workspace container and access, while workspace_data.py, graph_and_notes.py, and notebooks.py handle content. Imports chat_workspace and audit_log from eo, plus auth/user-lookup helpers from api/deps.
blocks.title: Module header and imports

blocks.text: Ten Pydantic request models covering every mutation shape. The comment block at lines 96-109 explains the owner_id naming convention: it really means the acting user's id and may be any role; the route just maps exceptions to HTTP codes.
blocks.title: Request models and route-level auth note

blocks.text: Six routes: list, create, get, rename, promote, and delete. promote_workspace contains the most branching: a session_id plus mode='partial' triggers chat_triggered_partial_promote (which fires notify()); any other combination calls promote(). FileNotFoundError maps to 404 throughout.
blocks.title: Core workspace CRUD

blocks.text: Four membership routes (get, add, update-role, remove). get_workspace_members fetches the workspace and its member rows separately, collects all user IDs including the workspace owner, looks them all up via the Admin API in one call, and assembles a flat list with owner first.
blocks.title: Membership management

blocks.text: Covers leave, forced owner removal (partner-only), vote get/cast, attribution toggle, and per-moderator attribution grant. get_workspace_audit at lines 387-418 adds the deletion-snapshot fallback: if member_role returns None it checks find_deletion_snapshot to see if the caller was an authorized viewer at deletion time.
blocks.title: Ownership transitions, voting, and attribution

blocks.text: GET /api/audit/me lives here even though it isn't under /api/workspaces because it shares audit_log with the workspace audit immediately above. No extra access check beyond require_auth: the query is always scoped to the caller's own user_id.
blocks.title: Self-scoped audit log

gotchas: The parameter named owner_id on every route is actually the ACTING user's id, not necessarily the workspace's owner — chat_workspace.py resolves true role internally
get_workspace_audit checks a deletion snapshot so the audit trail of a deleted workspace is still readable by those who had access at deletion time
promote_workspace has two code paths: chat_triggered_partial_promote (partial + session_id) vs promote (all other combinations)
how_it_works: Every route injects the acting user via require_auth (the owner_id parameter, which may be any role, not just owner)
FileNotFoundError from chat_workspace functions becomes 404; WorkspaceAccessError becomes 403; ValueError becomes 400
get_workspace_audit adds a deletion-snapshot fallback so a deleted workspace's audit trail stays accessible to people who had owner/partner access at the time of deletion
get_workspace_members enriches raw member rows with email/name/avatar_url via the Admin API before returning
outputs: workspace objects, member lists, vote status, audit log entries, action confirmations
purpose: Exposes every HTTP endpoint that governs the workspace container object and who-can-do-what-to-it. All workspace-scoped but non-governing endpoints (facts, graphs, notebooks) live in separate route files. Delegates all business logic to eo/chat_workspace.py and eo/audit_log.py, mapping their FileNotFoundError/WorkspaceAccessError to 404/403.
side_effects: writes via eo/chat_workspace.py (database rows for workspaces, members, votes, attribution)
Admin API call to look up user profiles in get_workspace_members
summary: FastAPI router for /api/workspaces: CRUD, chat attach/detach, membership, ownership, voting, attribution, and audit.
